label: Week 8 brief

storylines.title: Do not spot the worst team a half
storylines.fact: The Bengals had 59 yards in the first half at Baltimore, the fewest in any first half of a Burrow game [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50281493/jamarr-chase-fiery-half-speech-inspires-bengals-win). Tennessee led Cleveland 14–0 last week and still lost [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50239544/week-7-sunday-games-takeaways-questions-2026).
storylines.why: **Why it matters:** the Titans have not won two in a row since November 2022. They can steal a half. A slow start gives them the second one too.

storylines.title: Pressure Ward with four
storylines.fact: Cam Ward is pressured on 35.5% of dropbacks, averages 5.7 yards a pass and has five interceptions [Bengals.com](https://www.bengals.com/news/tennesse-titans-scouting-report-week-8-2026-game-preview). Tennessee's pass block win rate ranks 28th [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49742016/2026-win-rates-team-player-rankings-pass-rush-run-stop-blocking). Cincinnati pressures 39% of dropbacks while rarely blitzing [Bengals.com](https://www.bengals.com/news/tennesse-titans-scouting-report-week-8-2026-game-preview).
storylines.why: **Why it matters:** four rushers leave seven in coverage. A young quarterback under pressure with nowhere to throw is how this defence gets turnovers.

storylines.title: Pollard, not Ward
storylines.fact: Tennessee ran for 141 yards and three touchdowns in Cleveland [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50239544/week-7-sunday-games-takeaways-questions-2026). Cincinnati's run defence allows 34% success, third best, but runs off the offence's right tackle succeed 41% of the time, 25th, on 17 carries [stats page](https://petedilworth.github.io/bengals-fanzone/stats.html).
storylines.why: **Why it matters:** Tennessee has no passing game to fall back on. Stop Pollard early and its plan is gone.

storylines.title: Run wide left
storylines.fact: Tennessee allows 53% success on runs to the offence's left end (32 carries) and 47% at left tackle (17), but only 33% up the middle (49), fifth best. Cincinnati's best gap is left tackle: 50% on 14 carries [stats page](https://petedilworth.github.io/bengals-fanzone/stats.html).
storylines.why: **Non-obvious:** this is the reverse of last week. The middle that worked in Baltimore is Tennessee's strength. No outlet has mapped it.

storylines.title: Shotgun is who they are
storylines.fact: Burrow took three snaps under centre across the five touchdown drives in Baltimore [Bengals.com](https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-keep-their-cool-ravens-joe-burrow-jamarr-chase-zac-taylor). Play-action, the closest stand-in the line stats have, gains 0.07 expected points a dropback, 20th, against 0.23 without it [stats page](https://petedilworth.github.io/bengals-fanzone/stats.html).
storylines.why: **Why it matters:** a weak opponent tempts a coach back to his experiment. If the under-centre looks return with a lead, that is a choice, not a need.

watch.title: How many plays before the break
watch.text: Last week the Bengals ran 19 plays before half [Bengals.com](https://www.bengals.com/news/postgame-quick-hits-ja-marr-chase-second-half-stats-ravens-week-7-2026). A normal count means the slow start was Baltimore, not a habit.

watch.title: Which way the Bengals run
watch.text: The numbers point left, away from the middle. Count carries to each side of the line.

watch.title: Ward against a four-man rush
watch.text: Baltimore converted 9 of 16 third downs last week [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore/_/gameId/401873012), almost all before half. Watch if the four-man rush gets home before Ward finds the sticks.

watch.title: Pollard on the edges
watch.text: Watch where his carries go. Inside runs into Lawrence and Allen. Outside is where this defence has leaked.

watch.title: Under centre or not
watch.text: Count the snaps with Burrow under centre once Cincinnati is ahead. It shows what the staff still wants to test.

lineFinding: Last week this page said Burrow struggles when teams send five or more rushers. Baltimore did, on 11 of 32 dropbacks. The split moved from −0.11 to +0.04 expected points a dropback, now on 63 plays [stats page](https://petedilworth.github.io/bengals-fanzone/stats.html). One game turned a weakness into a wash. That is what a small sample looks like. Against four rushers, the offence still gains 0.25 on 166 plays.
devilsAdvocate: **A 1–6 team is not a free win.** Tennessee led Cleveland by 14 and lost by three [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50239544/week-7-sunday-games-takeaways-questions-2026). The line opened at Bengals by 6.5 and is now 12.5 [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/game/_/gameId/401873031/titans-bengals). Receiver Carnell Tate and back Tyjae Spears are out, but Ward and Pollard play [Bengals.com](https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-titans-week-8-2026-injury-report). If the rest of the move is a reaction to one half in Baltimore, the market may be overrating that half.
**The run-left map is thin.** It rests on 17 Titans carries and 14 Bengals carries at left tackle. A handful of plays could reverse it.

**The big second half may be the outlier.** Before Baltimore, Burrow's release was 2.57 seconds and the offence lived on short throws. One game at 3.06 seconds is not a new identity yet [NFL.com](https://www.nfl.com/news/week-8-nfl-mvp-tracker-joe-burrow-jared-goff-caleb-williams).

alternativeView.title: The same game, from Tennessee
alternativeView.text: From Nashville, this is a game to shorten. Run Pollard, keep Ward out of third-and-long and keep Burrow on the sideline. It worked in Cleveland for a half. The catch is the matchup: Cincinnati's run defence ranks third in success allowed [stats page](https://petedilworth.github.io/bengals-fanzone/stats.html), and Tennessee's run blocking ranks 30th by ESPN's win rate [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49742016/2026-win-rates-team-player-rankings-pass-rush-run-stop-blocking).
